basis: Gonadal dysgenesis and premature ovarian failure define endocrine gonadal dysfunction; isolated infertility subtypes do not negate this defining axis.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: gonadal dysgenesis and ovarian failure involve gonads as hormone organs; adrenal disease is not inferred from NR5A1.

basis: Spastic paraplegia, kyphoscoliosis and lateral tongue atrophy define the syndrome; lingual atrophy is structural oral involvement, annotated 30-79%, rather than dysphagia alone.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: defining lateral tongue atrophy directly affects an oral structure; the mouth belongs to gastrointestinal. Dysphagia alone would not qualify.

basis: HHV-8-associated B-cell lymphoma; malignant pleural and pericardial effusions each annotated 80-99%. Peritoneal occupation omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: malignant pleural effusion directly occupies the pleural cavity (80-99%); the underlying neoplasm arises from B cells rather than pulmonary tissue.

basis: Inherited proximal tubular wasting with metabolic acidosis. Rickets and leg bowing are reported, but subtype-specific prevalence >=30% or a required skeletal criterion is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: phosphate-wasting rickets is reported, but frequency is unspecified and it is not a required diagnostic criterion; >=30% is not established for this subtype.

basis: Lysosomal storage with defining neurodegeneration; dysostosis multiplex 16/16 and hearing impairment in roughly half. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.

decisions.otologic: involved: conductive and/or sensorineural hearing impairment affects roughly half over the usual course, exceeding 30%; it is part of the storage disorder.

basis: Amino-acid transport/endocrine disorder with cystinuria and defining neuromuscular hypotonia; developmental delay 7/7, seizures 5/7. One abnormal muscle biopsy does not establish common myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: primary: defining congenital hypotonia reflects neuromuscular dysfunction; developmental delay 7/7 and seizures 5/7 further establish neurologic disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hypotonia does not establish primary muscle damage; ragged-red fibers in one tested patient cannot establish common myopathy. No frequent skeletal lesions are documented.

basis: COFS defines cerebral, ocular and skeletal anomalies; microcephaly and arthrogryposis each 5/5. Microphthalmia is only 5-29%, but ocular disease is part of the syndrome definition.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular malformations define COFS and its syndromic-microphthalmia ancestry; the primary tier does not require microphthalmia itself to exceed 30%.

basis: T-cell deficiency defines an immune and blood-cell disorder; neutropenia occurs in 2/2. Vitiligo and alopecia are separately diagnosed autoimmune diseases; hepatomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the defining defect is in T blood cells, supporting the blood-cell mechanism axis; neutropenia in 2/2 provides additional evidence.
decisions.dermatologic: none: vitiligo and alopecia (each 1/2) are distinct autoimmune diseases associated with immune dysregulation, rather than direct skin damage from the T-cell deficiency.

basis: Callosal agenesis defines disease; scoliosis/hip abnormalities and strabismus occur in 30-79%, supporting skeletal and ocular dysfunction. Renal defects are 5-29%; optic atrophy frequency unknown.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus is a functional ocular abnormality annotated 30-79%; nystagmus is also frequent. This does not depend on the unspecified frequency of optic atrophy.

basis: Epibulbar lipodermoids and accessory auricular appendages define the syndrome. Preauricular tags are external-ear developmental anomalies; supernumerary nipples lie outside the axes.

decisions.dermatologic: none: preauricular appendages are accessory auricular structures; their skin covering does not independently establish a dermatologic disorder. Polythelia is outside the axes.
decisions.otologic: primary: preauricular appendages represent accessory external-ear structures and are a defining branchial-arch malformation.
